input: Draft a house emergency exit plan with kids

gold.taskTitle: Draft a Family Emergency Exit Plan with Kids
gold.taskDescription: Create a household emergency exit plan that accounts for the presence of children, covering escape routes, roles, and safety procedures.

questions.title: How many floors does your home have?
questions.description: Understanding the number of floors determines how many exit routes and escape scenarios need to be planned.

questions.title: How many children are involved, and what are their ages?
questions.description: The number and ages of children directly affect responsibilities, physical assistance needed, and how instructions should be communicated.

questions.title: What types of emergencies are you planning for?
questions.description: Knowing whether the plan targets fire, earthquake, gas leak, or multiple scenarios shapes which exit routes and actions are prioritized.

questions.title: Do any household members have mobility or medical needs?
questions.description: Any physical limitations or medical conditions among adults or children require specific accommodations in the exit plan.

questions.title: Do you have pets that need to be included?
questions.description: Pets add a layer of responsibility during evacuation and may require designated roles or equipment in the plan.

questions.title: Where is your planned outdoor meeting point after evacuating?
questions.description: A predetermined meeting point is a core element of any exit plan and affects how the route and roles are structured.

questions.title: Will adults always be home, or do kids need solo exit steps?
questions.description: If children may sometimes be home alone or with a babysitter, the plan must include age-appropriate independent evacuation instructions.
